01 / A PLACE FOR EVERY WINDOW

One screen.
Make room for more.

Drag a window to reveal the layout bar. Pick a position and let MacSnap snap it into place.

  • Halves
  • Thirds
  • Your way
  • Quarters

Want a shortcut? Drag to a screen edge or use Left, Right, Max and Center in the menu.

02 / TWO WINDOWS. ONE DIVIDER.

Resize one.
The other follows.

When two windows form a pair, the divider lets you change the balance between them. Drag to preview the new sizes, then release to apply them.

More room for whatever you're working on.

03 / YOUR WORKSPACE, YOUR WAY

A vertical screen.
Room for three.

macOS already offers half-screen and quarter-screen layouts. To make the most of a portrait display, MacSnap also offers vertical thirds: top, middle and bottom.

Editor at the top, browser in the middle, reference at the bottom. Choose a position for each window and keep all three in view, stacked one above the other.

Some apps enforce minimum window sizes, which can limit the layouts they fit into.

Download for macOS
  1. 01

    Download and unzip.

    Download the release ZIP and extract MacSnap.app.

  2. 02

    Move it to Applications.

    Move the app to your Applications folder and open MacSnap. You'll find it in the menu bar.

  3. 03

    Allow Accessibility access.

    In System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, allow MacSnap to arrange your windows.

Independently distributed.

The current release is ad-hoc signed and isn't notarized by Apple. macOS may show a warning when you open it. Read Apple's official guidance and only open apps from sources you trust.

BEFORE YOU START

A few
answers.

Still have a question?
Ask on GitHub ↗

Why did I build MacSnap?

After using other operating systems, I wanted more flexibility in how I arranged windows on my Mac. I found apps that could help, but some kept the features I wanted behind paid upgrades. That inspired me to build a native, free, open-source app, initially for my own use.

Which Macs does it support?

The universal download supports both Intel and Apple silicon Macs and requires macOS 13 or later. Snapping behavior can vary by app and display setup.

Is MacSnap free?

Yes. MacSnap is free to download, and the source code is available under the MIT license.

Why does it need Accessibility access?

macOS requires this permission so MacSnap can read window information, move windows and resize them in other apps. You can manage that access in System Settings.

How do I update it?

Download the latest release, quit MacSnap and replace the app in Applications with the new copy. The download button on this page always points to the latest release package.

What if a window won't fit?

Some apps set minimum sizes or restrict resizing. If something doesn't work as expected, open an issue with your macOS version, the app involved and the steps to reproduce it. Please leave out personal information and documents.
